clue.text: Missing article — Greek vase, first century: it could have been mothballed

definitions.note: a clause describing the substance rather than a bare noun

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word century

parts.note: the opening letter of century

indicators.note: an article is a word like a or the, and missing says it has been dropped from the vase

parts.note: a two-handled jar of ancient Greece
the indefinite article, here dropped

explanation.surface: A museum label notes an ancient Greek vase gone missing, perhaps packed away in storage.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards to the build: C first, then AMPHORA without its final A. 'Mothballed' looks like storage jargon but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mothballs were traditionally made from this aromatic waxy compound, so it is something that could have kept clothes protected from moths.

clue.text: Apt clue, maybe, for feuding family

indicators.note: maybe hints that the preceding words could be arranged some other way

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that this is a fitting clue for a family locked in a feud.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: 'Apt clue' is both the boast and the letters to rearrange into CAPULET.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet's household in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet are at bitter war with the Montagues.

clue.text: Chap in charge of English newspapers in downward movement has his ups and downs

definitions.note: a clause describing the person rather than a noun

indicators.note: in places the English newspapers inside the word for a downward movement

parts.note: a chap is a man
the standard abbreviation i/c
a plunge downwards, the outer piece
the usual abbreviation
the press, collectively

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss in a falling market finds his fortunes swinging up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ups and downs' sounds like business cycles but describes mood swings; i/c is the usual abbreviation for in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with this condition, now usually called bipolar disorder, swings between elated highs and despairing lows.

clue.text: Loud interruption to stop compassion is not altogether correct

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is a statement that is only partly true

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into something, so the loud letter goes inside the word for stop

parts.note: to halt is to stop; the outer piece
f, forte, the musical mark for loud
an old word for pity, as in ruthless

explanation.surface: Someone shouts to cut off a show of compassion, which turns out to be not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth, meaning pity, survives mainly in 'ruthless'; f is the musical mark forte.
explanation.definitionFit: A half truth is a statement containing only part of the truth, so it is accurate in some respects but misleading overall.

clue.text: Rising of the people or of the crown

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: lay means belonging to ordinary people rather than clergy or experts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A popular uprising is set against the crown, the people versus the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: LAY OR, read upwards, becomes ROYAL. 'Rising' looks like a revolt, which suits the people-or-crown picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal means belonging to the monarch, and the crown is the usual shorthand for monarchy itself.

clue.text: Trophy for railway used in theatre

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun

parts.note: a scalp taken as a trophy of victory
el is the American word for an elevated railway

explanation.surface: A railway company wins an award that it then displays in a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests a stage, but it is the operating theatre, where surgeons work.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small sharp knife is a basic instrument in the operating theatre of a hospital.

clue.text: Muscle inclined to pinch with rest — stopped up

indicators.note: inclined means tilted out of line, so the letters that follow are knocked out of order

parts.note: first part of the letters to rearrange
second part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A muscle tends to clench and relax in turn, leaving a passage closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopped up' adds to the definition rather than the wordplay: this ring of muscle closes an opening, and it does indeed pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphincter is a ring-shaped muscle that contracts to close a bodily opening or passage.

clue.text: Originally on top with new end

indicators.note: a new end means the last letter is swapped out for a different one

parts.note: above means on top of

explanation.surface: Something original is placed uppermost and given a fresh finish.
explanation.walkthrough: ABOVE has its final E replaced by O, giving AB OVO; the new end is an O, the shape of an egg, which fits a Latin phrase meaning from the egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means from the egg, that is from the very beginning, so it is used for going back to origins.

clue.text: Walked solemnly in front of important personage with treated food

parts.note: to process is to walk in a procession
a big cheese is an important person

explanation.surface: A dignitary leads a solemn parade while carrying some prepared dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Process with the stress on the second syllable means to walk in procession, which is the sense needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Processed cheese is cheese that has been industrially treated, blended and emulsified, a manufactured food product.

clue.text: Gamble with fate — have a go at keeping direction

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the direction goes inside the attempt

parts.note: to try is to have a go
east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A daring person takes a chance with destiny and tries their luck while staying on course.
explanation.walkthrough: Direction is one of the four compass points, here east.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a game of chance where prizes go by random draw, so entering one is a gamble.

clue.text: Decider could be fine — too reactionary to cry about

indicators.note: a reactionary wants to go back, so the word too is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a fine is a monetary penalty

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cry goes around the other piece

parts.note: to cry out is to shout; the outer piece
the word written backwards

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a fine is too backward-looking to be worth shouting about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like approval but is the punishment, and 'reactionary' turns only the word too.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn football or hockey match can be settled by a series of spot kicks, the tiebreaker that decides the winner.

clue.text: Student I quoted OK?

parts.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
taken as written
cit. is the abbreviation for cited, used in references

explanation.surface: A student asks whether it is acceptable to have quoted from a source.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a worry about plagiarism; L is the learner plate on British cars, and cit. is the scholarly shorthand for cited.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means allowed or lawful, so something licit is permitted and acceptable.

clue.text: Wheel finished before start of year in solitary

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word for solitary

parts.note: alone, the outer piece
finished means done

indicators.note: the start of a word is only its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A sentence of solitary confinement ends just before the new year begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solitary' suggests a prison cell; the answer is the giant observation wheel on London's South Bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Eye is a huge Ferris-style observation wheel beside the Thames, opened for the millennium.

clue.text: Vibrator made of aluminium partly put back in river

indicators.note: in places the portion inside the river

parts.note: an English river through Nottingham; the outer piece

indicators.note: put back means the portion is turned round to read the other way
partly says only a portion of the metal's name is wanted, the rest cut away

parts.note: only its first four letters are kept

explanation.surface: A vibrating gadget built partly of aluminium has been dropped back into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vibrator' wants to be something racier; it is an organ stop. The Trent is a major river of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremulant is an organ device that makes the notes waver, a mechanical vibrato producing a trembling effect.

clue.text: Tune up in real term connected with insurance

indicators.note: in places the tune inside the word for real

parts.note: real means actual; the outer piece

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A musician tunes up during a real school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tune up' looks like adjusting an instrument; 'term' looks like a school term but belongs to the definition, a word used by insurers.
explanation.definitionFit: Actuaries calculate risks and premiums for insurers, so actuarial describes insurance statistics and the vocabulary around them.

clue.text: Copper reserved for what's no trouble

definitions.note: a noun clause standing for an adjective meaning easy

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
shy and reserved both mean diffident

explanation.surface: A quiet police officer is kept back for a job that should cause no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Cushy is informal for easy and comfortable, so a cushy job gives its holder no trouble at all.

clue.text: Visit with Queen in central Scotland

definitions.note: a description of a place rather than a place name

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit
and means together with
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A trip in the company of the monarch to the heart of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Callander is a small town in Stirlingshire on the edge of the Trossachs, a place lying in the middle of Scotland.

clue.text: Chat show hostess's work gets a cheer

parts.note: op. is short for opus, a work
a shout of encouragement

explanation.surface: A television presenter's efforts are greeted with applause from the studio audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the hostess to her wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Oprah Winfrey hosted one of the most famous American daytime television talk programmes for twenty-five years.

clue.text: Slash brains? There's nothing Tory about that

parts.note: zero, shaped like O

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the political colour goes around the brains

parts.note: blue is the Conservative party colour; the outer piece
intelligence quotient, a measure of brainpower

explanation.surface: A sneer at cutting intelligence: there is nothing Conservative about such slashing.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative (Tory) party. 'Slash' looks like a cut but is the punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The forward slash character is also called an oblique or oblique stroke in British usage.

clue.text: Time everyone died, kept by uncle in slavery

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the uncle's name surrounds the preceding pieces

parts.note: Uncle Tom, from the Stowe novel; the outer piece
hr, the abbreviation for hour
everyone means all
d. is the genealogical abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Everyone died in captivity while held by an uncle, a grim family saga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' looks like T but here is HR. The uncle is Uncle Tom of Uncle Tom's Cabin, a novel about slavery, which suits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thralldom is the state of being a thrall, a bondsman or serf, so it means bondage or servitude.

clue.text: Objects to extraterrestrial attitude

parts.note: if one minds something, one objects to it
the film alien

explanation.surface: Someone resents having to adopt an alien's point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a habitual way of thinking, an established outlook that shapes how one responds.

clue.text: Security without tears, possibly — fail to follow

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so security wraps around

parts.note: a lock gives security; the outer piece

indicators.note: possibly says the word tears may appear in some other order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Feeling safe without crying, perhaps, means missing what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like not having, but here it is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose track of something is to stop keeping up with it, failing to keep following its progress.

clue.text: Excuse for not doing things thoroughly, addressed to London mayor

definitions.text: Excuse for not doing things thoroughly
definitions.note: a phrase describing a token effort, standing for the adjective

parts.note: taken as written
Ken Livingstone, Mayor of London from 2000

explanation.surface: A complaint about half-hearted work is sent to the Mayor of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone was London's first elected mayor when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A token gesture is a minimal one made for show, standing in for real, thorough effort.

clue.text: Executioner's boat

definitions.meaning: Jack ..., the notorious seventeenth-century English hangman

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive pretends the vessel belongs to a hangman; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ketch's name became a byword for the hangman, and a two-masted sailing craft shares the same name.

clue.text: Grey as a bird

parts.note: taken as written
a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: A simile: something is as grey as a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a comparison, but 'as' and 'a bird' simply join.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale grey like ash, typically describing a face drained of colour by shock.

clue.text: Little boy in living testimony to acuity

parts.note: as in the quick and the dead

indicators.note: in places the little boy inside the word for testimony

parts.note: to bear witness is to testify; the outer piece
short for Edward

explanation.surface: A small child stands as living proof of sharpness of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Quick in the old sense of alive survives in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity is keenness of perception or thought, the same as being sharp and fast in mind.

clue.text: Little boy in late return going on and on

indicators.note: in places the little boy inside the other word
a return goes back the way it came, so late is read the other way

parts.note: taken as written; the outer piece
Ernie cut short, a little Ernest

explanation.surface: A small boy comes home late yet again, and the scolding never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Compare 22-across, where the same phrase 'little boy' gave a different short name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever without end, something that continues endlessly.

clue.text: Runners coming about five — time to yield

indicators.note: coming about means turning around something, so the runners surround the five

parts.note: hares are fast runners; the outer piece
the Roman numeral
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Runners arrive around five o'clock and it is time to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yield' looks like a verb meaning give in; it is the noun, a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest is the crop gathered in a season, the amount the land produces.
